title: Replace continuous enqueue with event-driven coalescer and introduce KV slab-tiering
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: This ticket refactors the continuous enqueue/batching path to an event-driven coalescer and implements a two-tier KV slab allocator for hot/cold entries. Goals: reduce CPU churn from busy-polling, lower tail latency under mixed workloads, and improve KV hit-rate for long-running sessions. The change touches the request coalescer, admission controller, lease/heartbeat plane, and the KV store priming code.
acceptance_criteria: p95 generation latency reduced by >= 12% on mixed chat+inference benchmark compared to baseline
KV hot-tier hit ratio improves by >= 18% on our long-session load profile
CPU utilization for router/coalescer service drops by >= 20% under peak traffic in staging
All integration tests pass; canary rollout completed with automatic rollback hooks
No increase in error-rate (>= 99.99% success preserved) during 72-hour canary
tech_decisions: Adopt an event-driven coalescer: wake coalescer on incoming head-of-queue events and timer gaps instead of continuous enqueue polling
Introduce a lightweight per-shard slab allocator that maintains hot and cold lists; evictions move entries to cold-tier backed by mmap'd cold store
Decouple lease-probe heartbeat from admission controller: probe cadence reduced, use on-demand lease refresh for active sessions
Admission controller moves to soft-quotas + cooperative yielding instead of hard spinlocks to reduce contention
risks: Regression in throughput for extremely bursty traffic if coalescer wake heuristics are too conservative
Complexity in migration: mixed clusters might have old nodes expecting continuous enqueue semantics
Possible increase in cold-tier read latency until background priming reaches steady state
Edge cases around multi-tenant hotkey storms requiring emergency throttles
migration_steps: 1) Feature-flagged build: coalescer behind runtime flag 'event_coalesce_v2'
2) Deploy to staging and run long-running load generator (24h) against mixed chat and completion profiles
3) Enable KV slab-tiering in staging; run priming job and check metrics for hit ratio
4) Canary deploy to a small percentage of production namespaces; observe error-rate, latency, KV hit-rate for 72h
5) Gradually ramp canary (5% -> 25% -> 60%) with automated rollback on SLO breach
6) Once stable, flip default flag and schedule a post-mortem to capture metric deltas
rollout_plan: Week 1: Feature-flagged integration testing and internal perf runs
Week 2: Staging soak with production-like traffic generator; iterate on wake heuristics
Week 3: 72-hour production canary (low traffic namespaces), monitor, and collect profiles
Week 4: Ramp canary and full rollout if metrics meet acceptance criteria
testing_plan: Unit tests for coalescer state transitions and timer behavior
Deterministic sim tests for corner cases (idle -> burst -> idle)
Benchmarks: p95/p99 latency microbench for request aggregation; KV hit/miss microbench
End-to-end staging suite: mixed chat/completion with long session churn
Chaos: simulate delayed background priming and node restarts during canary
